package: W45-87 — the render-version and render-key layer
question: Which keys decide whether a surface re-renders, how does a component learn the current render version, and what does it mean for a drawn value to draw anything?
answer: 22 blocks are copied verbatim (2,667 units) into one module; the matcher runner gains seven verbatim blocks that restore its recovered semantics. A render key is `surface\0component\0requestId` (`MF`); the props key is `columns\0fullscreen\0sha256(props)` (`mIn`); the versioned key is `key\0\0<version>` only when the store holds the version of the versioned key (`jf(key)`, `$H`). `kVe` composes the two: it starts from the event counter `ui.render` and appends the version of the request key for this surface/component/request under the given viewport and props. `Tc` reads the whole render-version map (skipping the viewport key and the live/steady duplicates) or a listed set of keys under either pace. `wc` bumps one render version through the shared store; `Rc` is the state suffix, `kc` the live suffix, `wH`/`kH`/`xc` the live/steady key helpers and `Rb` the state-key test. `sur` sees a position or offset prop; `iur` draws a Box with one and recurses into Box children, but never for Text, Link or engine values; `$ur` reads a well-typed on-screen range or answers null/undefined.
measured: `$H(key, state, renderKey)` answers `KEY\u0000\u000011` when the store holds `jf(MF(input)) = 11` and the bare `KEY` when it does not; `jf` is `key + Rc` with `Rc = "\u0000state"`.
`mIn` splits into `["80","false",<64 hex>]` for viewport 80 columns, not fullscreen and props `{a:1}`; different props change the digest.

`Tc(state)` yields `ui.render\u00005\u0000K\u00002\u0000other\u00007\u0000` for the map with `ui.render=5`, the viewport key, `K=2`, `K live=3`, `S\0state=4` and `other=7`: the viewport key, every live key and every state-suffixed key are skipped.
`kVe(state, input)` is `5\u0000\u000011`; `wc("K")` moves K from 2 to 3 and touches no other key.

`sur({position})` and `sur({top:1})` are true, `sur({color})` and `sur(undefined)` false; `iur` is false for a string, an engine, a Text (with or without a `top` prop) and a Link, true for a Box with `top` and for a Box with a drawn Box child.
`$ur` returns `{first:1,last:2,of:3}`, null for an explicit null, and undefined for a missing or malformed range.
`j3e` is the eight message types; `Ioe` is `{type:"engine",ref:0}`; `Omt.defaultValue` is false; `l9.get()` is undefined before a viewport is written.
`WPn(input)` lists the modules that hook `ui.render` and match the component; `SVe` names them; `Frt(component)` answers whether any module hooks the event; `LAt` and `GPn` filter by an input.
`at` is sha256 hex and `eA` is its 64-hex test; `yno` memoizes the JSON id per object (equal objects share the id); `blt(undefined, ...)` is true (an absent matcher passes).

Matcher runner: `aUn(1,1)` true, `aUn(2,1)` false, objects match partially and recursively, aliases expand on either side (`Agent`↔`Task` via the names table), `Slt(/^x/,"x")` true and `Slt(/^x/,"y")` false; `b(undefined, ...)` is true.

partition.remaining: The terminal glue that renders a site through row accounting: `yt`, `pr`, the row helpers `lr`/`mr`/`fr`, `ur`, `cr`/`dr`, `xr`, `ar`, `$e`, `hdn`, `TU` and `VH`, with their imported row/draw accounting (`dce`, `g4n`, `pIn`, `uIn`, `Fss`, `che`, `Ioe`, `iur`, `$ur`, `mIn`, `kVe`, `OL`, `oIn`, `j3e`, `Frt`, `l9`, `Omt`).

blocks.note: `vA` — the render event name, `ui.render`
`rur`/`WPn`/`SVe` — match a loading module by event and component, the modules that hook the event, and their names
`GPn` — the hooks that hook the render event and match one component
`sur`/`iur` — whether props hold a position or offset, and whether a drawn value draws anything (a Box/Text/Link, recursively)
`wc` — bump one store key
`kc`/`wH`/`kH`/`xc` — the live-key suffix and the steady/live key choice
`Rb` — whether a store key is a version key
`oIn` — the viewport store key, `ui.render viewport`
`Tc` — the render version: the event counter and every key’s version, or the whole visible map when the key list is absent
`$H` — suffix a drawing key with its version
`MF` — the render key: surface, component and request id
`s_` — the registry’s plugin state
`hno`/`yno`/`mIn`/`kVe` — the memoized JSON id, the props key (viewport columns, fullscreen, props) and the render key with its version
`$ur` — the on-screen range a drawing reported, or null
`Frt`/`LAt` — whether any loaded module hooks the render event, and whether one hooks it and matches this component
`olt` — the offset prop names (top, left, right, bottom)
`j3e` — the message types a site answers
`Ioe` — the engine sentinel the glue draws when a render failed
`Omt` — the static-frame store
`l9` — the viewport store
`blt` — one matcher field check
`eA`/`at` — the sha256 shape and the sha256 id the props memo uses

decisiveFact: A render is versioned by the pair (event counter, per-request version entry): the counter says the surface changed at all, the request entry says this component must redraw, and the component key is stable across redraws. `Tc` deliberately drops the viewport key and every live/state-suffixed duplicate so the visible map is versioned by the steady keys alone. The package also proved the seam had resolved `l` to the wrong body: `aUn`/`Slt` answer through the recovered runner, which tests literal aliases through the names table and only matches an object matcher partially, so the previous mapping made every scalar matcher pass.

hostBoundary.surface: the shared render-version store and the module registry
hostBoundary.reason: The store is owned by the host (`it().renderVersions`, bound through `bindRenderVersions`) and read by name from the copied bodies; the registry supplies the hook list `Frt`/`LAt`/`WPn`/`SVe`/`GPn` filter. Both stay host seams; the copied bodies are the only readers.

changes.change: twenty-two copied blocks: the render event, the keys, the version readers, the drawing tests and the terminals of the render subsystem
the seam: the source names plus `renderEventName`, `renderKeyOf`, `renderKey`, `renderVersion`, `propsKey`, `onScreenRange`, `drawsAnything`, `renderEventHooked`, `renderEventHookedFor`
seven copied blocks restore the recovered matcher runner and its alias table; `l` now resolves to the runner instead of the seam helper
twenty tests: the keys, the drawing tests, the stores and sentinels, the hooks gates and the hash helpers
five regression tests: scalar equality, partial object matching, alias expansion, regex matching and the absent-matcher pass
